rubric.item: SPEC-13 correctness (every-push speed, spec section 9 target <= 15 s)

findings.issue: The every-push acceptance tests in this file take about 25 s together without coverage. Individual tests take 2.7-9.4 s (band edges 9.4 s, mixed spots 5.4 s, Maniac test style 4.5 s, SPEC-01 3.7 s, SPEC-10 2.7 s), and the builder reports 11-44 s each under coverage. FAST_TIMEOUT_MS is 120 s. This breaks the standing rule that speed or scale checks are opt-in and no every-push test should take more than about 10 s on CI. It also misses the spec's own section 9 target of <= 15 s total.
findings.evidence: npx vitest run on the four new and changed files: Duration 25.83s. check-styles tests 3683/4496/9386/5431/2687 ms. Runs: SPEC-01 does 2x500 + tally 500 + 300 + tally 300 hands. SPEC-04 does 2x1000. SPEC-05 does 3x2000 (soft). SPEC-07 does 3x1000. SPEC-10 does 1x2000. That is about 13,600 hands per push.
findings.fix: Lower hand counts and keep every assertion. I checked these counts with the CLI on seed 42: at 300 Mixed hands, TAG preflop-unopened is recommended 6 / alternative 2, all four styles have numeric aggression and Maniac is 83.8%. At 300 Soft hands, Calling station and Rock have numeric aggression. Use: SPEC-01 Mixed at 300 and plain at 100, asserting 'Style: TAG, 600 hands'. SPEC-04 at 300 (confirm Maniac VPIP is still < 50 with the deviation-free style). SPEC-05 Soft at 300. SPEC-07 at 300. SPEC-10: reuse a 300-hand Mixed run, or merge its assertions into SPEC-01's run so no extra run is needed. Lower FAST_TIMEOUT_MS to about 30 s. Target: under about 5 s total without coverage, with no single test over about 2 s. If the builder wants the original counts too, put them in a TLH_SLOW_TESTS-gated twin. Note: the spec names these hand counts, so the orchestrator should record this as a spec amendment. The assertions themselves don't change.

findings.issue: The byte-identical-to-main check of ci.yml, million.yml and million-lineups.yml catches its own failure and skips when the `main` ref is missing. CI checks out with actions/checkout at the default fetch-depth 1, so on PR and branch pushes the ref is missing and the assertion never runs there. It only runs locally. After merge, this check (in a locked test) fails on any future branch that legitimately edits ci.yml or the million workflows, because the working tree then differs from `main`. A one-time scope check for this task has become a permanent ban on editing those workflows.
findings.evidence: onMain() returns null on any git error, and line 63 has `if (committed !== null) expect(...)`. ci.yml has no fetch-depth, so it uses a shallow single-ref checkout. Nothing in the repo uses the `git show main:` pattern elsewhere (grep under tests/ci, tests/git and tests/toolchain).
findings.fix: Remove the onMain loop (lines 16-27 and 61-64) from the permanent test, and leave the 'ci.yml, million.yml, million-lineups.yml unchanged' check to the judge's one-time `git diff --stat main` (SPEC-14 already does the same kind of check). The test is locked, so this needs the routine locked-test re-pin, and the SPEC-12 bullet should be marked as verified by the judge instead.

findings.issue: SPEC-11 says the exit code is 0, but the test never records a non-zero exit as a failure. It only collects 'Outside band:' lines when code != 0, so a non-zero exit from some other cause is covered only indirectly by other assertions.
findings.fix: Push `seed ${seed}: exit ${run.code}` into failures whenever run.code !== 0, and keep the Outside-band lines for context.

findings.issue: 1,059 lines changed against a scope budget of 850 (about 25% over). Most of the excess is test code. The 9 changed files match the budget.
findings.evidence: gates/fix-2.json changed_lines 1059; spec 2 'Scope budget: files=9, lines=850'.
findings.fix: Shrinking the fast tests (the first finding) and removing the onMain helper (the second finding) will bring this down. No other action needed.

findings.issue: StyleCheck(false) still builds the per-style mixed-spot maps on every hand's first sight of a style, even though they are only read under --check-styles. It's harmless, but the class does slightly more work than the flag needs.
findings.evidence: The mixedCounts initialisation is not guarded by recordMixed.
findings.fix: Optional: keep it as is (it's simple). Or store recordMixed and skip the mixed-map setup when it is false.

summary: The implementation is correct against every SPEC item. Shared style-stat functions are used and there is no own action counting outside the A-4 advice comparison (AC#11). Attribution goes by per-hand lineUp with the user seat excluded and all seats counted as TAG without a line-up (A-1): the 2000-hand Mixed CLI run sums the TAG seats to exactly 5535. Violating and abandoned hands are skipped and the step buffer is always cleared (A-2). The band check uses the rounded value with inclusive edges (AC#2). Aggression excludes preflop through handStyleCounts (AC#3). Mixed classification copies decideTag's draw condition: chart basis, alternative not null, spot marked in mixedSpots, move.type versus alternative (A-4/A-6). A mutation that drops the alternative-null guard is caught by the unit test. The style block sits after Line-up and before Bot results. Exit codes: 1 for violations or a failed check, 2 for usage, and replay mode is unaffected. The dispatch-only workflow would run without an `npm ci` step: `npm run playtest` is `node --import resolve-ts.js` using Node 22.18 built-in type stripping, and none of the transitive src/playtest, bots, advice, engine or stats modules import an npm package. million.yml and million-lineups.yml have the same layout, and `npm run playtest -- --hands 2000 --lineup mixed --size 6 --check-styles` ran fine under plain node, exiting 1 with a correct failure block. Two MAJOR findings: (1) the every-push acceptance tests take about 25 s, against the user's opt-in speed rule and the spec's 15 s target, and lowering them to about 300 hands keeps every assertion; (2) the workflow test's `git show main:` comparison is skipped in shallow CI checkouts and, after merge, would fail any future legitimate edit of ci.yml or the million workflows. Side observation, not a code defect: at 2000 hands on seed 42, TAG aggression (67.2%) and Rock aggression (55.6%) were outside their bands. Whether the 100k seeds pass is for SPEC-11 and the judge to confirm.
